Index Calculus Leaderboard

Every curve this repository has priced end to end, with the best index-calculus recipe measured on it, against Pollard rho on the same curve and the same point. The units differ between the three tables below, and so do the references and the floors: S and the ratios are comparable inside a table and nowhere else. Cold, set-up included, no row is below its reference. On one unseen point of a Koblitz curve (table A) the index calculus's online interval is 10.2–26.5× faster than rho once its reusable set-up exists, but the set-up is paid first: cold it is 5.23–21× slower, and a generic walk given the same precomputation would be 1.42–3.52× faster online again (a model). Prime and random-binary curves (table B), one target each: 5.47× to 13.5× and 10.6× to 38.2×.

New n37 counted diagnostic, outside the priced tables

On icv1-f2m37-tm534059-32aad96b, shared-rank K16 has 1,184 actual usable points and 16 folded columns. In 40 verified one-target runs, mean cold counted S is 2.111 as a lower bound; its counted IC/rho quotient is 5.034, and K16/K42 is 0.349. Both arms leave native work unpriced, and L0 timing gives no admitted online speedup. These figures are not comparable to tables A–C. Frozen decision. A separate whole-solve Callgrind census finds K16/K42 = 0.367 and K16/rho = 4.461 in simulated instructions on eight paired points; native wall and online speed remain unknown. Raw instruction replay.

Untouched n37 K8/K16 instruction confirmation

On icv1-f2m37-tm534059-32aad96b, K8 has 592 usable points and 8 folded columns. Across 16 new same-point public workloads, K16/K8 whole-solve Callgrind Ir is 1.190 [1.158, 1.222], selecting K8 for the cold implementation route. K8/rho is 3.645 [3.235, 4.136] in the same instruction unit. All 64 profiles and 320 independently replayed measured records verified. This is not isolated online wall speed; K16 remains a target-only candidate. Frozen decision.

Fresh n37 K8/K16 target-only instruction gate

On icv1-f2m37-tm534059-32aad96b, K8/K16 target-only Callgrind Ir is 2.886 [1.730, 4.602], so the frozen gate prioritizes K16 for an isolated n37 online wall test. K16/rho target-only Ir is 0.153 [0.092, 0.240], but K8/K16 complete-solve Ir is 0.848. All 64 profiles and 320 independent native replays verified. Callgrind Ir is simulated instruction work, not isolated wall speed; n41/n53 and ECC2K-130 transfer stay open. Frozen decision and raw replay.

Hosted n37 native wall screen: L1 diagnostic

On icv1-f2m37-tm534059-32aad96b, all 320 measured executions replayed on another host class. For preregistered one-target workload Wd281dbafa0cb, descriptive rho/K16 online wall is 7.178. Across the separate 16-target panel, K8/K16 online wall is 7.110 [3.669, 16.982]. All rows earned L1, and the identical K16 A/A maximum deviation was 12.85%, above the frozen 5% gate. No online speedup is admitted; carry K8 and K16 to an L2 host and n41/n53. Frozen decision.

Complete n9 F6-IC control, outside the priced tables

On icv1-f2m9-tm5-4a3ea183, all three arms recovered the logarithm of public point [305, 466] after building 14 usable base points, collecting 8 verified ordinary relations and solving 2 folded columns. Inherited F4, F6-IC and matrix F5 inside-worker cold times were 4.707, 3.150 and 61.937 ms; their one-target online times were 0.372, 0.272 and 3.118 ms. Independent replay checked all scalars, relations, column logs and phase totals. These are exploratory L0 Mac wall observations on a tiny subgroup. With no same-target rho reference or fully priced operation count, IC/rho speedup and S remain unknown. Keyed measurements · independent replay.

F6-IC E_0 ladder in ecbench, outside the priced tables

#1333's inherited-F4 and F6-IC decomposers ran unmodified in ic.pipeline beside same-target strong rho on eight public one-target workloads per size. IC S is a lower bound: the solver's word XORs are counted but unpriced, and F6-IC's geometric point additions are charged. The F6-IC word-XOR saving vanishes once the base exceeds #1333's 256-point closure cap; charging its geometry makes the trade a relabelling. Decision: not decidable: fewer than six targets completed at some size, or fewer than four sizes (m = 31 incomplete). Analysis.

The board

One row per curve: its best recipe, ranked within its table by the cold ratio to that table's reference, the whole method from set-up to a verified logarithm. There is no single unit here. Tables A, B and C below are priced in different units against different references and floors, stated at the head of each; S, × ref and × floor are comparable inside a table and nowhere else. Tables A and B solve one target per row, as AGENTS.md's one-target rule requires: A on one unseen public point per process against one-target rho on the same point (§23's comparison, re-run at the ic tool programme's baseline v3, 64 points per size, §23's figures kept as the before marks), B against the matched negation-map rho (ledger §18). Table C is a historical 32-target diagnostic. For the Koblitz rows of A the online interval, the reading with rho at the canonical step and the generic-precomputation model sit beside the cold ratio, as §23 requires. The bar splits S into phases. A walked-target row on the ladder is resolved to about a factor 1.8 either way at three repetitions (ledger §13.7).

Each dot is a ratio to its own table's reference, in that table's unit; the three rows of dots are not comparable with one another.

Reusable set-upCurve and subgroupWorkflow constructionsFactor basePair tableRelations (PDP)Linear algebraDescentVerification

Table A · Koblitz, one target §23, re-run at baseline v3

Unit
one batched affine addition (add_many over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r. A clock reading, not a count: ic price times each phase exclusively, on one thread, and divides by this unit, measured around each repetition (§20, §23). Each process measures its own unit, which is 2.3–3.2 times cheaper at baseline v3 than in §23's processes, so S here is not compared with §23's; the ratios carry no unit (research/ic_tool_program/rule/v3/README.md).
Reference
One-target rho on the same point, measured as built (its set-up plus its walk), in the same unit and the same process; its answer replayed and verified (§23; rule v3 at baseline v3).
Floor
√(π/4n) rho steps per √r: generic, one target, no precomputation, A = 2n by signed Frobenius and negation, n the extension degree. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, so × floor here divides units by steps.
Targets
one unseen public point per process, 64 per size; §23's figures on the same curve are the before marks
Status
primary comparison: one target, as AGENTS.md's one-target rule requires
Rho step
rho's walk as built costs 9.72–11.8 units a step; the canonical step costs 4.6–5.39

Table C · Koblitz, 32 targets in a batch §19–§22

The collection thread's rounds before §23 solved 32 targets together and priced them per target against batch rho on the same 32 (§19–§22). Under the one-target rule that is a historical diagnostic, not a primary comparison; it is kept here with its §21 figure as the before mark and the one-target cold ratio §20 derived from this run (shared phases plus one mean descent, against single-target rho), which table A's measured figure replaces. The phase split is the most detailed the thread has.

Unit
one batched affine addition (add_many over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r, per target. A clock reading, not a count: ic price times each phase exclusively, on one thread, and divides by this unit (§20, §22 isolated re-run).
Reference
Batch rho on the same 32 targets (signed Frobenius and negation), its counted operations priced at the canonical step, one batched addition plus the table canonicalisation, in the same process (§20). Collisions shared across the 32 targets are in its cost per target.
Floor
L(32)·√(π/4n) steps per √r per target, with L(32) = 0.19869: the one-target floor of table A times Kuhn–Struik's batch share. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, and a smaller object than table A's floor, so × floor in C and in A do not compare.
Targets
32 targets solved together, priced per target
Status
historical diagnostic under AGENTS.md's one-target rule: 32 targets solved together
Rho step
the canonical step costs 1.8–2.3

Every recipe on every ladder curve

Table B only: ratio to the matched rho for each variant the ladder ran, three repetitions averaged. The minimum per curve is the row on the board. The balanced recipe sizes the base at the family optimum F = (c·#E·t/k)1/3, which is 0.75·r1/6 in S on a prime-order curve (ledger §11.2): a rising cost against a flat reference, so this family has no crossover to find at any size.

The ECDLP, step by step

What each phase computes, what it costs, and how fast it grows. The exponent α is the fit of that phase's operations to rα on the Round-5 ladder (table B, in GAE) for the balanced recipe; rho grows as r1/2, so a phase with α above ½ loses ground at every size. The share columns are the phase's part of S on each family's leading row.

At the Koblitz batch headline (§22) the pipeline stored 265,680 pairs, collected 86 relations from 2,017,897 scanned summands, reduced 86 rows to a Wiedemann core of dimension 12, and spent 24,134 descent trials per target. Koblitz top-end exponent, ratio·√n against r over the four largest sizes: β = 0.137 [-0.0592, 0.332], against the law's 1/6 and the model's 0.141; it cannot yet tell them apart. The ladder's rho fits sit under ½ because set-up still shows at these sizes (ledger §18.5).

The point decomposition problem, per target

Every oracle answers the same question on the same Semaev systems: is this target a sum of m base points? Cost is group-addition equivalents per target, found and refuted averaged; FFD is the first fall degree of the Weil-restricted system. The pair table answers in 0–25 units where F4 needs 102–106 and SAT more, which is why the board's recipes use it. Zero disagreements on every cell.

Every curve the repository names

Native analysis and source records

N83 Tier 1 cold factor-base holdout

Five sealed one-target points; 25 independently replayed IC arms and five same-point rho solves on one GitHub-hosted cloud instance. K1152 ran A/B on each point. The frozen selection status is BOUNDED_UNKNOWN; selected candidate null.

K1120 saves 2.645 s against K1152 (paired 95% 2.085 to 3.205 s). Its 0.401 s advantage over K1104 has a 95% interval of -0.236 to 1.038 s.

The cold interval includes base and index construction, relation rank, target recovery and producer verification. Rho starts with its target-dependent walk and ends after scalar verification. This Tier 1 wall-time panel uses its own unit and sits outside the operation-unit S rankings.

Frozen IC1 rows and candidate identities

What this is not. A view of frozen measurements, class accounting: no row here was measured for this page, and nothing is a speedup.
